bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds deployed for capacity expansion, backward integration, and debt reduction (repaid INR 311cr debt at ~8.5-9% cost). INR 200cr general corporate purpose utilized for working capital. Net debt reduced to INR 135cr.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delay in PM-KUSUM 2.0 announcement impacting H1 FY27 revenue; Elevated receivable days (155 days) due to state agency payment cycles; Geopolitical volatility driving raw material costs; Execution risks in new rooftop/C&I segments; Competitive pricing in tenders.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural demand and policy support; Conservative on near-term (H1) guidance due to execution uncertainty in new segments and scheme timing; Aggressive on capacity expansion and backward integration; Emphasizes 'transitionary' nature of margin pressures.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management views inverter production not as a standalone revenue stream but purely as a backward integration tool to control quality and protect project margins, avoiding the cut-throat standalone inverter market. The INR 116cr post-balance sheet collection fundamentally alters the cash flow narrative, proving underlying cash generation is strong despite reported negative OCF.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- IPO proceeds were used to de-lever: the full INR 2,800.00 mn for pre-payment/repayment of the Company's borrowings and the full INR 310.00 mn for repayment of Oswal Solar's borrowings were utilised as on 30.06.2026.
- Net debt to equity fell from 1.21x (FY24) and 0.99x (FY25) to 0.08x (FY26), rising to 0.15x at Jun'26; net debt to Operating EBITDA moved 1.45x / 1.09x / 0.26x to 0.90x (annualised) at Jun'26.
- Balance sheet remains working-capital heavy: net current assets of INR 14,554 mn versus total assets of INR 22,821 mn at 30-Jun-26, with total borrowings rising from INR 2,253 mn (31-Mar-26) to INR 3,076 mn and cash and cash equivalents falling from INR 907 mn to INR 413 mn.
- Returns have normalised post-IPO equity raise: RONW 88.7% (FY24), 93.0% (FY25), 35.7% (FY26) and 12.7% annualised at Jun'26; ROCE 57.7% / 64.6% / 37.4% and 15.8% annualised.
- Shareholding as on June 30, 2026: Promoter and Promoter Group 75.7%, DIIs (MFs, AIFs) 5.5%, Body Corporates 3.2%, FIIs 0.1%, Others 15.6%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Solar Pumping: Core driver, awaiting KUSUM 2.0; Magel Tyala orders pending allotment. Rooftop Solar: Entered via PM Surya Ghar; SPV formed for Rajasthan govt buildings (HAM model). Module Mfg: Expanding 600MW to 2.1GW with backward integration (extrusion, EVA). Inverters: Internal production starting in 6-7 months for captive use.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as "One of the Fastest Growing Vertically Integrated Solar Pump Manufacturer in India", citing a 54.7% CAGR in terms of revenue growth "during the last five fiscals" and "23+ Years" of experience in pumping solutions spanning engineering, product design, manufacturing and testing.
- Claims to be "one of the largest suppliers of Turnkey Solar Pumping Systems under the PM KUSUM scheme", noting it emerged as one of the largest suppliers of solar powered agricultural pumps under PM KUSUM "within six years" of entering the segment.
- Operates a three-way route to market under PM KUSUM: turnkey systems supplied directly to farmers, turnkey systems supplied to other players participating in the scheme, and solar pumping systems supplied only as product to such players.
- Retail reach rests on an "extensive distributor network across India" of 1,406 distributors as of June 30, 2026.
- "Why Oswal Pumps?" is framed on vertically integrated manufacturing, enhanced engineering and design capabilities, comprehensive product portfolio, extensive distribution, strong presence in major agricultural belts of India, experienced management, industry tailwinds and government-scheme opportunity.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Scheme risk] Management flags "the delay in the rollout of PM KUSUM 2.0" as the trigger for diversification, and industry-wide competitive bidding under Magel Tyala as the cause of a 9% fall in realisations.
- [Receivables] The lengthening receivable cycle is attributed to "delays in payments from state nodal agencies"; management expects normalisation over the medium term, leading to lower cash conversion cycle and "in turn, lower interest costs".
- [Accounting change] "Pursuant to amendments in Ind AS 107 and Ind AS 101, suppliers' credit has been reclassified from other current financial liabilities to current borrowings", which affects the total borrowings and net debt series.
- [Market context] The deck cites public sources for India's solar market: FY26 total ~45 GW across all segments, Utility Scale's share ~47%, Rooftop ~20% (PM Surya Ghar driven) and C&I and KUSUM ~17% each, with installed base milestones of "First 50 GW - 11 Years, Next 50 GW - 3 Years, Last 50 GW - 14 Months".
- [PM Surya Ghar progress] As on 07.08.2026 the scheme reports ~7.80 Mn applications, ~4.23 Mn installations, ~5.07 Mn households covered, ~15.01 GW capacity installed and ~INR 285.16 Bn subsidy released; Union Budget 2026-27 allocated INR 22,000 crore to it.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margin moderation (23.2%) due to competitive tender pricing and geopolitical input cost inflation. FY27 guidance 22-23% reflects transitionary headwinds. Mitigation via value engineering and backward integration (modules, structures, upcoming inverters).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 20-25% in FY27 (back-ended, H1 flat/decline, H2 acceleration); EBITDA Margin: 22-23% (FY27, pressured by geopolitics/competition); Order Inflow: Dependent on PM-KUSUM 2.0 announcement (expected June); Capex: INR 350cr in FY27 (INR 90cr parent automation, INR 260cr solar module expansion to 2.1GW).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 19,912 executable pumps (covers Q1 FY27); Near-term pipeline >25,000 pumps (converts over 3-4 months); Cumulative executed: 106,122 systems across 15 states; Rooftop/C&I/Utility pipeline: ~300 MW.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: PM-KUSUM 2.0 scale-up (FY27+); 300 MW non-pump solar pipeline (Rooftop/C&I/Utility); Capacity expansion enabling INR 6,000cr+ peak turnover potential; Inverter backward integration to protect margins.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Oswal Pumps delivered record FY26 profitability (PAT +34% YoY) driven by PM-KUSUM execution, but guides for a back-ended FY27 (20-25% growth) due to timing gaps before PM-KUSUM 2.0 rollout. Strategic diversification into rooftop/C&I solar and deep backward integration (modules, upcoming inverters) aims to de-risk single-scheme dependency, though near-term margins face pressure from geopolitical input costs and competitive tendering.
